# SQLx compilation fixture

This opt-in crate pins SQLx 0.8.6, with PostgreSQL, query macros and Tokio support,
in its own lockfile. It does not add SQLx to semblock's dependency graph.
The edition-2021 upstream crate is MIT OR Apache-2.0; this fixture selects MIT.
SQLx 0.8.6 declares no formal MSRV; its complete locked graph is built on the
repository's Rust 1.88 baseline. SQLx 0.9 requires Rust 1.94, so it is not the
baseline fixture. The project remains actively maintained at
<https://github.com/launchbadge/sqlx>.

All seven SQL expressions are copied verbatim from the existing Go project or
`tests/go_string_coverage.rs`: all six reviewed macros plus a chained query
function. `schema.sql` provides only the table/column descriptions needed by
the compiler; the test never executes these queries.

The four `.sqlx/query-*.json` files were generated by real SQLx macro compilation
against PostgreSQL 18 using `schema.sql`, for both the original and formatted
query spellings. They are not handwritten descriptions. Formatting changes
SQLx's query-text hashes, so both versions need metadata for this offline test.

From the repository root:

```text
cargo fetch --locked --manifest-path tests/fixtures/rust-sqlx-project/Cargo.toml
cargo test --locked --test rust_project_integration actual_sqlx -- --ignored
```

The integration test copies the crate, builds before and after formatting with
`SQLX_OFFLINE=true`, `DATABASE_URL` removed, and locked offline Cargo resolution,
then checks whole-file goldens and idempotence. Its explicit opt-in keeps normal
CI network-free. PostgreSQL is not required to run the committed test.

To regenerate metadata after changing a query, create an isolated database from
`schema.sql`, set `DATABASE_URL`, `SQLX_OFFLINE=false`, and `SQLX_OFFLINE_DIR` to
this fixture's absolute `.sqlx` path, and run `cargo check` on both the input
crate and a formatted copy. Review metadata and goldens together. SQLx's MIT
license is supplied with the downloaded dependency; no upstream code is copied.
